host.description:
The URL of your dedicated Lucca account: `{account}.{env}.{region}`.

Account reflects your company name. Env indicates the environment. Region depends on your server location.

**Please, use your test or sandbox environments (and not your production env.) for testing purposes.**

Environments:
- `ilucca`: production environment for customers.
- `ilucca-test`: test environment for customers.
- `ilucca-demo`: demo environment for prospects.

Regions:
- `.ch` for Swiss located accounts.
- `.net` for the others.

Regarding sandboxes, the pattern differs: `https://{account}-{sandboxName}.sandbox.{server}.luccasoftware.com`, where:
- `{sandboxName}` is automatically generated upon creation.
- `{server}` may be "eu1", "eu2" or "ch1".

oAuth.description: The Lucca API implements the [oAuth 2](https://oauth.net/2/) protocol with the [client-credentials-flow](https://auth0.com/docs/get-started/authentication-and-authorization-flow/client-credentials-flow). Refer to RFC8725.

scopes.employee-personal-records.readonly:
Read [employee-personal-records](/api-reference/latest/employees/employee-personal-records).
This contains highly sensitive data about the personal detail of the person.
scopes.employee-personal-records.readwrite:
Create, update or delete 
[employee-personal-records](/api-reference/latest/employees/employee-personal-records).
This contains highly sensitive data about the personal detail of the person.
scopes.leaves.readonly:
Read access to the leaves management system.
Gives read access to:
- the `leave` resources,
- the `leave-account` resources,
- the `leave` employee's name.
scopes.leaves.readwrite:
Read and write access to the leaves management sub-system.
Gives the same read access than `leaves.readonly`.
Also gives write (create, update and delete) access to the `leave` resource.
Also indirectly gives access to:
- leave employee's time unit (days, hours) for errors management,
- leave employee's work contract dates for errors management.
scopes.leave-requests.readonly:
Read access to the leaves approval workflow management sub-system.
Gives read access to:
- the related `leave` resources,
- the related `leave-account` resources,
- the related `leave` employee's name,
- the `expectedApprover`'s name.
scopes.leave-requests.readwrite:
Read and write access to the leaves approval workflow management sub-system.
Gives the same read access than `leave-requests.readonly`.
Also gives write access to the `leave-request-decision` resource.
scopes.webhook-deliveries.readwrite: Send a ping event to a webhook-endpoint.

include.description:

    May be `null` when you do not have access to the resource (or action).
  - `totalCount`: only applicable on collections (i.e. lists of resources), gives
    the total number of items across all pages.

Read more about [expanding responses](/documentation/using-api/includes).

sunset.description:
The **Sunset** response header (see [RFC 8594](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8594)) indicates the point in time at which this endpoint or resource will become unavailable. The sunset value is a timestamp [RFC 9110 Section 5.6.7][rfc-9110-5.6.7] that usually points to the future. If a sunset value points to the past, then the endpooint or  resource must be expected to become unavailable at any time.
As an API client, you should monitor the presence and value of all **Sunset** headers  and be ready to take counter measures.

legal-entity.title: legal-entity
legal-entity.description:
Representation of a legal entity, i.e. an organization that is subject to legal responsibilities in a given jurisdiction (country).

A legal-entity may be comprised of several [business-establishments](/api-reference/2024-11-01/organization/business-establishment) which represent geographically localized structures where the actual work is done. One of which is marked as the legal-entity headquarters.

legalName.description: **Must be unique**. Legal name of the legal-entity.

remoteId.description: The third-party API ID of the matching object.

isArchived.description: If this legal-entity is archived. Only possible if there are no more business-establishment attached.

taxIdentificationNumber.description:
Identifier of the legal-entity in its local jurisdiction.
- France: SIREN (Système d'identification du répertoire des entreprises)
- Germany: SN (Steuernummer).
- Spain: N.I.F (Número de Identificación Fiscal)

industryCode.description:
The industry (classification) code identifies the main type of activity of this legal-entity.
- France: APE or NAF code.
- Spain: CNAE.
- Germany: WZ (Die Klassifikation der Wirtschaftszweige).
- U.S.A.: NAICS (North American Industry Classification System).

postalCode.description:
Optional. Postal code of the address. Not all countries use or require 
postal codes to be present, but where they are used, they may trigger 
additional validation with other parts of the address 
(e.g. city validation).

locality.description:
Optional. Generally refers to the city/town portion of the address. 
Examples: French city, IT comune, UK post town.

administrativeArea.description:
Optional. Highest administrative subdivision which is used for postal 
addresses of a country or region. For example, this can be a state, 
a province, an oblast, or a prefecture.

business-establishment.title: business-establishment
business-establishment.description:
A business-establishment is a geographically localized unit of the organization structure.

It belongs to a [legal-entity](/api-reference/2024-11-01/organization/legal-entity). A legal-entity may have one (and only one) business-establishment set as its headquarters.

Business-establishments are an essential resource of the enterprise model, as they are the fundamental units of access rights scoping. As such, most objects are either directly or indirectly attached to a business-establishment.

Employees are attached to a business-establishment through their job-position.

remoteId.description: The third-party API ID of the matching object.

isArchived.description: If this business-establishment is archived. Only possible if there are no more employees attached.

legalEntity.description: Reference to the [legal-entity](../organization/legal-entity) this business-establishment belongs to.

isHeadquarters.description:
True when this business-establishment should be considered the headquarters of the legal-entity it belongs to.
A legal-entity may only have a single one headquarters.

taxIdentificationNumber.description: - France: SIRET (Système d'identification du répertoire des établissements). Must start with the same identifier than its legal-entity (SIREN).

industryCode.description:
The industry (classification) code identifies the main type of activity of this legal-entity.
- France: APE or NAF code.
- Spain: CNAE.
- Germany: WZ (Die Klassifikation der Wirtschaftszweige).
- U.S.A.: NAICS (North American Industry Classification System).

business-establishment.embedded.description:

Only returned if requested by the API client: `?include=embedded`.

legal-entity.description:
Legal-entities the business-establishment(s) belong to (cf. `businessEstablishment.legalEntity`).

Structured as a dictionary of [legal-entities](../organization/legal-entity) indexed by ID.

department.title: department
department.description:
A department represents a subdivision of the employee workforce, most often erected around 
the type of activity they do.

Departments are a tree-like structure, as any department may be child to another.

Note: contrary to most resources, departments are not attached to business-establishments.
This means:
  - business-establishments listed in access rights management do not affect departments.
  - employees may work in different business-establishments (or even legal-entities) and yet
    still belong to the same department.

remoteId.description: Identifier of this object in a third-party software.

isArchived.description: If this department is archived. Only possible if there are no more employees attached.

parent.description: Reference to the department this department is a child of.

level.description: **Read-only.** Depth level of this department in the department tree. At level "1", the department has no parent.

manager.description: Reference to the employee that acts as the Head of this department.

sortOrder.description: Index (0-based) of the department among its siblings.

activeEmployees.description: Link to the paginated list of active employees currently positioned in this department. List may be partial due to insufficient access rights.

totalCount.description: Total number of department resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

t9n.title: Translations
t9n.description:
Used for translation purposes. Object is structured as a dictionary whose keys refer to translated properties of the parent object, and whose values are a dictionary of supported languages.

On the parent object, the translated property value is considered the "invariant" translation. It is expected to show this value whenever the user's language has no translation in `t9n`.

Languages are identified through their RFC 4646 language tag.

occupation-category.title: occupation-category
occupation-category.description:
The occupation-category resource represents a categorization of employees belonging to a set of business-establishments.

These categories can be used as a way of distinguishing employees in reports, or may be used to specify reserved business rules (e.g. in the leaves management system).

In France, can be used to represent the "Profession et Catégories Professionnelles" (P.C.S.).

title.description: **Must be unique**. Invariant name of this occupation-category. Can be translated through `t9n.title.{langTag}`.

businessEstablishments.description:
`null` value **MUST** be interpreted like "ALL business-establishments, even those that will be created further down the line".

As a result, array cannot be empty.

job-qualification.title: job-qualification
job-qualification.description:
A job-qualification is an object that represents an employee profile regarding their skillset.

It is composed of both:
- a [profession](./profession), which indicates the nature of their job.
- a rank (number), which indicates either their level of expertise or of responsibilities in the company.

title.description: **Must be unique.** Invariant name of this job-qualification. Can be translated through `t9n.title[{langTag}]`. Leading and trailing spaces are automatically removed.

rank.description: The lower the rank, the "lower" in the company's hierarchy (i.e. the CEO is at max rank). Maximum rank can be set trough configuration.

totalCount.description: Total number of job-qualification resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

job-qualification.embedded.title: job-qualification.embedded
job-qualification.embedded.description: No embedded resources on a job-qualification(s) response. Expect an empty object if embedded are requested.

employee-status.title: employee-status
employee-status.description:
**Read-only.** The employee status is calculated from the employee's [employments](../employments/employment).
- active: employee has an employment as of today.
- upcoming: employee currently has no employment but will have one in the future.
- deactivated: employee used to have an employment but no longer does.

x-enumDescriptions.active: Employee has an employment as of today.
x-enumDescriptions.upcoming: Employee currently has no employment but will have one in the future.
x-enumDescriptions.deactivated: Employee used to have an employment but no longer does.

daterange.description:
[ISO 8601 formatted date-range](/documentation/using-api/filtering#dates-date-times-and-date-time-offsets) string.
Examples:
  - `2024-01-01--2024-12-31`: from Jan. 1st 2024 until Dec. 31st 2024 (included). 
  - `..--2024-12-31`: until Dec. 31st 2024.
  - `2024-01-01--..`: from Jan. 1st 2024.

employee.title: employee
employee.description:
The employee represents the public face of an employee in the system. Note that an employee can also represent a trainee, an intern, a contractor, etc...

The `applicableEmployment` property references the employee's [employment](../employments/employment) that is:
- currently in effect if the employee is "active".
- will first be in effect if the employee has an employment starting in the future (either the first or a new one).
- was last in effect if the employee is no longer employed and is not expected to be re-remployed in the future.

The `applicableJobPosition` property references the employee's [job-position](../employments/job-position) that matches the same logic.

portrait.description: Reference to the employee's portrait, which is a file (picture) representing them.

givenName.description: Name given at birth. In the U.S.A., the first name of a person. In French: "prénom". Leading and trailing spaces are automatically removed.

familyName.description: Name inherited from the person's family. In the U.S.A., the last name of a person. In French: "nom (de famille)". Leading and trailing spaces are automatically removed.

email.description: Professional email of this employee. "<" and ">" characters are forbidden. Some domains are blacklisted and may thus result in 400 errors.

birthDay.description:
Year-less date of birth.

**Read-only**, as it is infered from the employee-personal-record `birthDate`.
Take note that `month` starts at "1" and not zero, i.e. "1" is for January, "2" for February, etc...

day.description: Starts at "1". Maximum depends on the month.

month.description: Starts at "1" and goes up to "12" (included).

phoneNumber.description: Professional phone number of this employee.

applicableEmployment.description:
**Read-only.** Reference to the applicable [employment](../employments/employment) of this employee.
If the employee status is "deactivated", then references their last employment.
If the employee status is "upcoming", then references their closest next employment.

applicableJobPosition.description:
**Read-only.** Reference to the active [job-position](../employments/job-position) of this employee.
Matches the same logic as the "applicableEmployment".

totalCount.description: Total number of employee resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

employment.title: employment
employment.description:
The employment resource represents a relationship between an [employee](../employees/employee) and a [legal-entity](../organization/legal-entity) over a continuous period. It may actually represent a work contract, an internship agreement, a contractor's contract, etc...

The actual job of the employee is defined through the [job-position](/api-reference/latest/employments/job-position) resource, which references an employment. Over the course of his/her employment, the employee may occupy several job-positions.

remoteId.description: Resource identifier in a third-party system.

legalEntity.description: **Read-only**. Reference to a legal-entity. Inferred from the business-establishment of its first job-position.

date.description: Date of the first day (included) of this employment.

Date of the last day (included) of this employment. After this date, this employment is considered terminated.

Leave `null` for permanent employments (as long as the employee is kept), and set the date of the last day in case of a fixed-term employment.

EndsOn date must be greater or equal than StartsOn date.

jobPositions.description: Link to the related [job-positions](../employments/job-position) for this employment.

probationaryPeriods.description: Link to the related probationary-periods for this employment.

job-position-changed-attributes.title: job-position-changed-attributes
job-position-changed-attributes.description: List of attributes that can change for a job-position.

job-position.title: job-position
job-position.description:
The job position represents a stage in an [employee](../employees/employee)'s career during one of their [employment](/api-reference/latest/employments/employment) in a given [business-establishment](../organization/business-establishment).

It therefore outlines the attributes of the person as a professional (qualifications) and their role in the company as well as who's their manager.

remoteId.description: Resource identifier in a third-party system. No unicity constraint: two job-positions may have the same value.

startsOn.description:
Effective date of this job-position for this employee.

Cannot be outside the range of the employment.

This should be considered "applicable" based on the related [employment](../employments/employment) business-establishment timezone.

endsOn.description:
**Read-only.** End date (included) of this job-position effectiveness.

Is calculated from the `startsOn` property of the closest next job-position, or the `endsOn` date of the parent employment.

This should be considered "applicable" based on the related [employment](../employments/employment) business-establishment timezone.

Must be greater or equal than StartsOn date.

jobTitle.description: Short description of the job occupied by this employee.

manager.description: Reference to another employee, who is considered to be this employee's manager.

notes.description: Optional notes about this job-position change.

updatedAttributes.description: List of attributes that changed compared with this employee previous job-position, even if said job-position was on another employment and/or not immediately sequential.

leave.title: leave
leave.description:
A leave is a period an employee takes off work while he should otherwise be working. 
Employees are entitled to these either by law or by contract.

### The leave-account & details

A leave references a [leave-account](./leave-account) which represents the type of leave: annual 
leaves, maternity, sick leave, etc... The leave-account determines:
1. The unit (days, hours) of any leave taken on this leave-account.
2. Whether some extra **details** are needed on leave taken on this leave-account. For example, companies 
in France are required to give a lot of details when it comes to sick leaves. Otherwise, these details
should be left `null`.

### The leave status

The leave status indicates whether the leave resource should be considered valid (i.e. the company management
gave its approval) or not.

### The leave-request

A leave may be subject to an approval process by the management. In this case, it must be created with
the "pending" status (an "approved" leave needs no further approval) which then automatically creates 
a [leave-request](../leave-requests/leave-request) for this leave.

If a leave is created with an "approved" status, then it has no leave-request, and its status may then
be changed directly through a PATCH request. The only available status would then be "cancelled".

### Half-days of absence

An employee may work in the morning, and take the afternoon off, and vice versa. The `startPosition` and
`endPosition` attributes represent this behavior. For example, taking the Jan. 2nd afternoon off:

```json
{
"startsOn": "2023-01-02",
"startPosition": "secondHalfDay",
"endsOn": "2023-01-02",
"endPosition": "secondHalfDay"
}
```

startsOn.description: Date (only). First day (included) of this employee's leave.

startPosition.description:
Does this leave start on the first half-day
(often: "morning") or the second one (often: "afternoon")?

endsOn.description: Date (only). Last day (included) of this employee's leave.

endPosition.description:
Does this leave end on the first half-day
(often: "morning") or the second one (often: "afternoon")?

days.description:
**Read-only.** Lists the days or half-days (when on two different leave-accounts) of absence.
It is automatically calculated by the server depending on the leave-account 
settings (e.g. should Saturdays be included?).

range.description:
Range over which the leave spread on this day.
- `firstHalfDay`: Only covers the first half of the day (often: the morning).
- `secondHalfDay`: Only covers the second half of the day (often: the afternoon).
- `allDay`: Covers the whole day (often: both the morning and the afternoon).

x-enumDescriptions.firstHalfDay: Only covers the first half of the day (often: the morning).
x-enumDescriptions.secondHalfDay: Only covers the second half of the day (often: the afternoon).
x-enumDescriptions.allDay: Covers the whole day (often: both the morning and the afternoon).

allOf.description:
Depending on the related leave-account, a leave may be taken in hours or in days.
This attribute sums up the duration of the leave on all of the days it covers.
Can only be written on when creating a leave in "hours" unit.

Some [leave-accounts](/api-reference/2024-11-01/leaves/leave-accounts) required further details about the leave.
This is typically the case for sick leaves in France. In this case, set these details in this object.
Otherwise, you can just leave this `null`.

lastUpdatedAt.description: Timestamp of the time this leave was last updated.

allOf.description: Link to the related leave-request (approval process) if it exists.

Link to approve the leave-request (POST) if there's a pending related leave-request. 
It may need multiple approvals from different employees.

Link to deny the leave-request (POST) if there's a pending related leave-request. 
A single denial is enough.

totalCount.description: Total number of leave resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

leave-account.title: leave-account
leave-account.description:
A leave-account represents a type of [leave](./leave) taken by your company [employees](../employees/employee). 
Common examples are: annual leaves, sick leaves, maternity, casual leaves, etc...

unit.description:
Indicates which days should be included over the leave period, as well
as the unit of the leave duration (fraction of days VS number of hours).
- `workingDays`: Entire half days on any day the employee should work on.
- `workingHours`: Part of a half day on any day the employee should work on.
- `businessDays`: All days the employee should work one, plus Saturdays (6-days week).
- `calendarDays`: All days, Sundays and holidays included.

x-enumDescriptions.workingDays: Entire half days on any day the employee should work on.
x-enumDescriptions.workingHours: Part of a half day on any day the employee should work on.
x-enumDescriptions.businessDays: All days the employee should work one, plus Saturdays (6-days week).
x-enumDescriptions.calendarDays: All days, Sundays and holidays included.

business-request-status.title: Business Request Status
business-request-status.description:
Describes the status of the request in regard to the approval process.
- `pending`: Request has not yet been approved by all expected decision-makers.
- `approved`: Request has been approved.
- `denied`: Request has been denied through a denial decision.

x-enumDescriptions.pending: Request has not yet been approved by all expected decision-makers.
x-enumDescriptions.denied: Request has been denied through a denial decision.

leave-request.title: leave-request
leave-request.description:
A leave-request is the resource that represents the state of the approval process of one
or more [leave](../leaves/leave) resources. You can only create leave-requests containing a 
single leave through the Lucca API, but when created through the app, you can expect a 1-N 
relationship between leave-requests and leaves.

The leave-request `status` attribute indicates the final result in regards to the approval process.

Approval is the result of the decision-making process of one or more employees. The list
of expected decision-makers is determined by the application settings.

Each expected approver makes his/her decision, which results in the creation of a [leave-
request-decision](./leave-request-decision) resource.

leaves.description: List of leaves this leave-request contains. Usually, a single one.

expectedApprover.description: Employee who is expected to take a decision regarding this leave-request.

totalCount.description: Total number of leave-request resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

employee.description:

leave-request-decision.description:
A leave-request-decision represents the decision of management regarding the status of a [leave-request](./leave-request). The approver may either approve the request, or deny it. In the latter case, the leave-request is marked as rejected, and no further decisions are required. Otherwise, other managers approval may be asked, leading to futher decisions.

The `type` property indicates whether the decision is an "approval" or a "denial".

An extra `comment` property is required in the case of a denial.

Note: this decision-making process is sequential: no two managers may be expected to approve a leave-requeest at the same time.

event.title: event
event.description: Represents a change made to the state of a resource.

id.description: Unique string identifier of this event.

url.description: Absolute URL for the event resource.

apiVersion.description: API version of the resource representation contained in data. Not to be confused with the API version of the representation of this present event, which is indicated in the `Api-Version` HTTP header.

allOf.description: Indicates which type of event occurred. Usually concatenates the name of the object type with the kind of change ("created", "updated" or "deleted").

occurredAt.description: Timezoned timestamp of the moment when this event occurred.

source.description: URL of the tenant. Ensures unicity of {source} + {id}.

data.description: Representation of the resource whose change triggered the event. Please note that this is the representation of the resource just after the change, and it may have changed again since then.

businessEstablishment.description: Business Establishment of the Resource in the Event, if there is one.

previousAttributes.description:
Only sent on `*.updated` event topics. Keys are the list of modified attributes. Values are the values of these attributes before the change.

This is only available for some resources. If a value in the dictionary is NULL, then it can either mean that the original value was NULL or that we can't retrieve them for this Resource.

totalCount.description: Total number of event resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

cloudevent.title: cloudevent
cloudevent.description:
This is a [CloudEvent](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec) compliant representation 
of a [webhook-delivery](#schema/webhook-delivery).

id.description:
Identifies the Event.
Event producers MUST ensure that the source and id
combination is unique for each distinct Event.

type.description:
Indicates what type of event occurred.
Please refer to https://developers.lucca.fr/event-types
in order to view all supported event types.
Is prefixed with a reverse-DNS name.

source.description:
Identifies the context in which an event happened: the
API endpoint that hosts the collection of resources the
affected resource belongs to.

comluccasoftwarefirstdeliverytime.description: Timestamp of the first delivery attempt (UTC).

comluccasoftwarelatestdeliverytime.description: Timestamp of the latest delivery attempt (UTC).

comluccasoftwaredeliveriescount.description: Number of times this event has been attempted to be delivered.

comluccasoftwarewebhookendpointwebhooken.description: The webhook-endpoint that gave way to this Event being delivered.

comluccasoftwarewebhookendpointurl.description: URL of the webhook-endpoint that gave way to this Event being delivered.

cloudevents.title: cloudevents
cloudevents.description: Representation of a collection of event objects that conforms to the CloudEvents standard.

webhook-endpoint.title: webhook-endpoint
webhook-endpoint.description:
A webhook-endpoint describes the endpoint on your side that will receive events from your Lucca account.

It must handle HTTPS and support POST requests.

It should always check the signature of received events in order to increase security.

It should respond as fast as possible, otherwise, the server may stop sending it events.

Please refer to the [webhooks documentation](/documentation/webhooks) to learn more about webhook-endpoints.

webhookUrl.description: URL of the receiving endpoint on your side. MUST use the `https://` schema.

topics.description: See complete [list of all topics](../events/event) in the event definition.

businessEstablishments.description: Restrict events to those belonging to one of the given business-establishments. `null` should be interpreted as "all business establishments".

status.description:
'active': delivery attempts will be executed.
'suspended': if too many errors are	encountered on delivery. Completing the activation challenge is required.
  Events are kept in history
'inactive': events are neither sent nor kept in history

x-enumDescriptions.suspended:
Events are not be delivered but are kept in history. In order to resume delivery, 
first send a confirmation event.
x-enumDescriptions.ianctive: Events are neither sent nor kept in history.

totalCount.description: Total number of webhook-endpoint resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

webhook-endpoint.embedded.title: webhook-endpoint.embedded
webhook-endpoint.embedded.description: No embedded resources on a webhook-endpoint(s) response. Expect an empty object if embedded are requested.

webhook-delivery.title: webhook-delivery
webhook-delivery.description: A webhook-delivery is the object that represents the job to send an event to a [webhook-endpoint](./webhook-endpoint). It will lead to one or more [webhook-delivery-attempt](./webhook-delivery-attempt).

nextAttemptAt.description: Timestamp of the next planned webhook-delivery-attempt (UTC).

attemptsCount.description: Number of times this event has been attempted to be delivered.

status.description: Indicates whether the event has been delivered or not.

x-enumDescriptions.undelivered:
Webhook-delivery failed but a new
webhook-delivery-attempt is scheduled.
x-enumDescriptions.failed:
Webhook-delivery failed and no new
webhook-delivery-attempt will be made.

totalCount.description: Total number of webhook-delivery resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

Embeds the representation of resources related to the webhook-delivery(ies).

Only returned if requested by the API client: `?include=embedded`.

event.description:
Webhook-event(s) that are the payload for these deliveries (cf. `webhookDeliveryAttempt.webhookDelivery.event`).

Structured as a dictionary of [(webhook-)events](../events/event) indexed by their ID.

webhook-delivery-attempt.title: webhook-delivery-attempt
webhook-delivery-attempt.description:
A webhook-delivery-attempt is an attempt to send an [event](../events/event) to a [webhook-endpoint](./webhook-endpoint).

For any [webhook-delivery](./webhook-delivery), there may be multiple webhook-delivery-attempts, as the webhook service will retry sending an event if the webhook-endpoint fails to respond successfully.

totalCount.description: Total number of webhook-delivery-attempt resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

webhook-delivery.description:

Structured as a dictionary of [webhook-deliveries](../webhooks/webhook-delivery) indexed by their ID.

event.description:
Webhook-event(s) that are the payload for these deliveries (cf. `webhookDeliveryAttempt.webhookDelivery.event`).

Structured as a dictionary of [(webhook-)events](../events/event) indexed by their ID.

400.description:
Bad request. You may:
  - (write requests) make sure the request body conforms with the expected schema.
  - double check all required parameters are set.

example.title: One or more validation errors occurred.

endsOn: Invalid period: StartsOn should be before EndsOn.
employeeId: The employeeId query parameter is required.

401.description: You are not authenticated. Please refresh your token.

403.description: You do not have the required oAuth scopes.

404.description: Not Found. Resource may have previously been deleted.
